Corollaries — one per clause of the shipped rule. (i) Re-tier per sub-task. The index is \(\rho_i(t)=c_i/p_i(t)\): prices are global but success probabilities are per-sub-task. If sub-tasks \(t,t'\) order two tiers oppositely (\(\rho_i(t) \lt \rho_k(t)\) but \(\rho_i(t') \gt \rho_k(t')\)), any single session-wide order inverts the pair \(\{i,k\}\) for one of them, hence is not \(\rho\)-sorted for that sub-task; a non-sorted order has an adjacent strict inversion, and when that slot is reachable the exchange of Lemma 2 strictly saves — the session-wide order strictly overspends there. (ii) Reserve the strong tier — by index, not exception. On ambiguity, architecture and security sub-tasks \(p_{\text{cheap}}(t)\) is small, so \(\rho_{\text{cheap}} = c_{\text{cheap}}/p_{\text{cheap}}\) blows up past \(\rho_{\text{strong}}\) and the sorted cascade opens with the strong tier: dispatching straight to strength on hard calls is the same index policy. For irreversible actions, let a tier-\(i\) miss additionally cause expected damage \(d_i\) before the verifier catches it; every occurrence of \(c_i\) in the spend formula and in Lemma 2 becomes the expected outlay \(\tilde c_i = c_i + (1-p_i)d_i\), the entire argument runs unchanged, and the inflated index \(\tilde\rho_i=\tilde c_i/p_i\) pushes damage-prone cheap tiers behind the strong one. (iii) Escalate on a verified miss, never a hunch. Modify the optimal cascade so that at a slot \(j\) with nonempty continuation the agent, with probability \(\beta \gt 0\), escalates without consulting the verifier. With probability \(q_j\,\beta\,p_j\) a genuine success is discarded and the continuation spend \(W_{j+1} \gt 0\) (positive since all \(c_i \gt 0\)) is paid needlessly: the expected excess \(q_j\,\beta\,p_j\,W_{j+1} \gt 0\) whenever slot \(j\) is reachable, and the discarded success is recovered only if a later tier passes, so the guarantee cannot rise — hunch-escalation is dominated on both coordinates. Dually, accepting on a hunch at the same slot \(j\) — stopping unverified with probability \(\alpha \gt 0\), blind to the attempt's true outcome — costs nothing when the attempt happened to succeed but strands the sub-task when it failed: it lowers the success probability by \(q_j\,\alpha\,(1-p_j)\,S_{j+1}\), where \(S_{j+1}\) is the continuation's success probability — positive here, since the continuation is nonempty and every \(p_i \gt 0\) — and so exits the equal-guarantee class altogether whenever slot \(j\) is reachable. (At the final slot the continuation is empty and \(S_{K+1}=0\); there a blind accept instead swallows the fallback \(F\), reporting an unverified outcome as done — it violates the class's stopping rule directly rather than through the guarantee.) Hence verified-miss escalation is the only admissible trigger in the class, and among admissible policies the Theorem selects the index cascade. \(\square\)

In fabius. R11 dispatches each sub-task to the \(\rho\)-minimal tier and lets R8's verdict — never a vibe — trigger the climb. "The cheapest tier that holds" is exactly the condition that the price order and the \(\rho\)-order coincide: mechanical, tightly-contracted work has \(p_{\text{cheap}}\approx 1\), so \(\rho_{\text{cheap}}\approx c_{\text{cheap}}\) and stays cheap, while ambiguity, security calls and irreversibility inflate \(\rho_{\text{cheap}}\) (through small \(p\) or damage \(d\)) and route to strength via the same single threshold \(W \gt \rho_i\) that R3 applies to calls and R2 applies to ladder rungs.

Boundary. PROVED, under the stated model: Lemmas 1–2, the Theorem, the threshold/EVOI form, and corollaries (i)–(iii) — assuming (A1) attempt outcomes independent across tiers, (A2) a sound and complete verifier with its cost folded into \(c_i\), (A3) known, calibrated \((c_i, p_i(t))\), (A4) risk-neutral expected spend with one attempt per tier. What remains operational heuristic: independence (A1) is load-bearing — real tier failures correlate through latent sub-task difficulty, a cheap-tier miss is evidence lowering every untried tier's posterior success probability, and under correlation the static index policy loses its optimality proof (recomputing indices on posterior probabilities is the sensible move, but no optimality is claimed here, and optimal correlated sequencing is intractable in general); same-tier retries are the maximally correlated case and sit outside the model. Corollary (iii) prices a hunch-escalated attempt at the full \(c_j\) — verification folded in per (A2) — so a policy that skips verification precisely to recoup its cost sits outside the model and is not dominated by this argument; it is excluded on other grounds (an unverified pass certifies nothing). R8's real verifier is only approximately sound and complete — a false pass erodes the "same success guarantee" clause at a rate this entry does not bound. The indices themselves are estimates: the theorem is conditional on calibration, and no robustness bound for misordered \(\rho\)'s is proved. Which sub-tasks count as "ambiguity / architecture / security" is a classification judgment about where \(p_{\text{cheap}}\) is small, not a theorem. Finally, the source survey's savings figures (arXiv 2601.14192) are task- and dataset-specific; what transfers — and what is proved — is the index/threshold form, not any particular cost number.

title: Dual exit gate + hard cap: the long-horizon step→verify loop as optimal stopping
issues: Dependence factor claimed '1 <= kappa' in general — false: the Fréchet lower bound permits kappa < 1 under negative dependence. Fixed to the full Fréchet range with positive dependence (shared source) identified as the failure direction that climbs toward the min bound.

Claim that the martingale regime 'produces flat windows at rates the null cannot' is false in general — a nonnegative martingale can show flat windows with probability below L^w. Fixed: the isometry fires the window with probability 1, the martingale regime contains the isometry so admits no bound below 1; the test is now honestly framed as size <= L^w under the null, power 1 against the stalled-at-fixed-distance alternative, unquantified against slow leaks.

'Contraction reaches e_k <= tol within ceil(...) cycles' overstates a stochastic (expectation) contraction — only E[e_k] decays geometrically; sample-path arrival needs a Markov tail. Fixed to expectation + geometrically decaying tail bound.

Escalation-folding parenthetical claimed 'the same algebra returns the same threshold form' — untrue without an extra hypothesis, since min is concave and the exact test is a value-of-information inequality. Fixed: explicit posterior-resolving-gate assumption yields q_k + (1-q_k)p_{k+1} > c_cyc/c_esc, the same form with a strictly stricter constant; otherwise only the VoI inequality holds (same safe direction). Boundary updated accordingly.

'Unique undominated policy' fails at threshold ties (stop and continue tie at equality) and p_{k+1} is undefined on {q_k = 1}. Fixed: ties broken toward stopping (the safe tie-break), convention (1-q_k)p_{k+1} = 0 on {q_k = 1} added to the Setting.

Reflection-test step 'posterior unchanged hence p_{k+1} = p_k' used a hidden assumption; made explicit that the next attempt is drawn by the same policy from the unchanged cause-posterior, hence has the same success law.

Optimality telescoping silently assumed a constant per-cycle cost while the Setting allows c_cyc in [c_min, c_max]; scoped to constant cost with the F_j-measurable varying-cost generalization noted, and the Boundary now states the optimality claim's exact scope (declare-done terminal loss + constant per-cycle cost).
Placement string contained a literal '>' ('p > c/V'); rewritten without angle brackets per house style.
Theorem (iii) optimality claim now explicitly scoped to the declare-done terminal loss so the theorem statement matches what the proof establishes.

Optimality claim was false at the cap boundary: 'no optimal rule stops off S' and 'any rule differing from it off ties is dominated' are contradicted by trajectories that never enter S by cycle N — at j=N the harness forces every rule, optimal ones included, to stop off S. Fixed by qualifying 'before the cap' and restating the optimum as first-crossing-or-cap.

The folded-escalation parenthetical claimed 'the constant moves in the safe direction', implying the folded rule is uniformly stricter than the plain one; in fact the left side also gains the resolution term q_k, so under a posterior-resolving gate the folded rule can correctly continue where the plain rule stops (counterexample: q_k=0.5, c_esc/W=0.5, c_cyc/W=0.05 — plain test needs p>0.1, folded test q+(1-q)p>0.1 always passes). Fixed to state both changes explicitly and disclaim uniform strictness.

The Boundary repeated the vague 'same safe direction' claim for the general value-of-information inequality and left ambiguous whether first-crossing optimality extends to the folded (escalate-inclusive) loss; fixed: the folded test is established at one-step lookahead only (closed form only under a posterior-resolving gate), and first-crossing optimality is proved for the declare-done loss alone.

Three wording overstatements tightened: Statement (i) attributed the multiplicative false-alarm drop to 'separately sourced' (the operational proxy) where the proof requires conditional independence; Statement (ii)'s 'hypothesis test of size L^w against R8's contraction' could be read with contraction as the alternative rather than the null; and 'holding a run-level budget ε forces the per-cycle rate below ε/N' presented a sufficient condition from a union bound as a necessity.

Verified sound and left untouched: the min/union/Fréchet bounds and the κ range endpoints (min/(αCαD)=1/max(αC,αD) checked); the Bayes-factor identity under two-sided conditional independence; the run-level union bound; deterministic termination, cost ≤ N·c_max, rollback ≤ r; the conditional-Markov stall-test size L^w (threshold e_k is F_k-measurable and positive, e_k=0 case handled) with power 1 against the fixed-distance stall and no sub-1 bound in the isometry/martingale regimes; the absorption identity (1-q_k)(1-p_{k+1}) via the tower property; both threshold algebras including the q_k=1 convention and the tie at equality; the posterior-resolving evaluation q+(1-q)p>c_cyc/c_esc (re-derived, correct); the telescoping optional-sampling argument with {σ>j}∈F_j and bounded increments on the finite horizon; and E[σ*]≤W/c_min plus the 1/m tail. No literal < or > appears inside math — all comparisons use \lt/\gt.
html:
Statement. For multi-cycle autonomous work, run the fabius-disciplina step → verify cycle as a stochastic loop with exactly three exits: stop-done at the first cycle where the completion condition \(C_k\) and an explicit, separately-sourced done-signal \(D_k\) hold simultaneously; stop-escalate on a certified stall; and a hard cap of \(N\) cycles, rate-limited and checkpointed. We prove three things. (i) The conjunctive gate \(C_k\wedge D_k\) never has a higher false-stop rate than either signal alone, shrinks it multiplicatively when the two signals are conditionally independent — the design target that separately sourced operationalizes — and pays at worst an additive price in missed stops; over an \(N\)-cycle horizon exactly this shrinkage is what keeps the run-level false-stop probability bounded. (ii) The loop terminates surely with deterministically bounded cost and bounded state corruption, and both stall tests are inherited objects: the no-progress window is a hypothesis test whose null is R8's contraction and whose size is at most \(L^w\), and the repeated-cause reflection test is M4's redundancy lemma verbatim. (iii) The whole rule is one expected-loss threshold — continue iff \((1-q_k)\,p_{k+1} \gt c_{\mathrm{cyc}}/W\), M4's threshold functional applied to the disjoint variable pair (completion belief, per-cycle hazard) — and with the hard cap making the horizon finite, under a monotone (diminishing-returns) hazard this myopic threshold is the exact optimal stopping rule for the shipped declare-done loss, not merely a heuristic.

Setting. Cycles \(k=1,2,\dots\) are adapted to a filtration \((\mathcal F_k)\). Let \(T_k\) be the event that the task is truly complete after cycle \(k\); completion is absorbing, \(T_k\subseteq T_{k+1}\). Write \(q_k=\mathbb P(T_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\) (completion belief) and \(p_{k+1}=\mathbb P(T_{k+1}\mid eg T_k,\ \mathcal F_k)\) (per-cycle hazard); on \(\{q_k=1\}\) the hazard is vacuous and we adopt the convention \((1-q_k)p_{k+1}=0\). Each cycle emits two stop signals: \(C_k\), the verify condition read from the objective verifier, and \(D_k\), an explicit done-signal from a distinct channel (sentinel marker, independent checker, human ack). Error rates, taken uniform across cycles: false alarms \(\alpha_C=\mathbb P(C_k\mid eg T_k)\), \(\alpha_D=\mathbb P(D_k\mid eg T_k)\); misses \( eta_C=\mathbb P( eg C_k\mid T_k)\), \( eta_D=\mathbb P( eg D_k\mid T_k)\). Costs: per-cycle cost \(c_{\mathrm{cyc}}\in[c_{\min},c_{\max}]\) with \(c_{\max}\) enforced by the rate limit; \(W\gt 0\) the loss of a false stop (handing off incomplete work as done); \(c_{\mathrm{esc}}\in(0,W)\) the cost of escalating. From R8 reuse the progress metric \(e_k=d(x_k,x^{\ast})\ge 0\), the distance of the working state to the verify condition's fixed point.

Theorem. (i) Gate. Unconditionally \(\mathbb P(C_k\wedge D_k\mid eg T_k)\le\min(\alpha_C,\alpha_D)\). If \(C_k\perp D_k\mid eg T_k\), it equals \(\alpha_C\alpha_D\), strictly below the min whenever both rates lie in \((0,1)\); meanwhile \(\mathbb P( eg(C_k\wedge D_k)\mid T_k)\le eta_C+ eta_D\). Over a run of at most \(N\) gate evaluations the run-level false-stop probability is at most \(N\alpha_C\alpha_D\) (dual, independent) versus \(N\alpha_C\) (single). (ii) Termination. \( au=\min( au_{\mathrm{gate}}, au_{\mathrm{stall}},N)\le N\) surely; total cost \(\le N c_{\max}\); a runaway rolls back at most \(r\) cycles of state, \(r\) the checkpoint interval. If the loop still contracts in R8's sense (\(\mathbb E[e_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le L\,e_k\), \(L\lt 1\)), a \(w\)-cycle no-progress window fires falsely with probability at most \(L^w\). (iii) Threshold and optimality. One-step lookahead yields the policy: continue iff \((1-q_k)p_{k+1}\gt c_{\mathrm{cyc}}/W\), with ties broken toward stopping — at equality the two actions tie exactly, and stopping is the safe tie-break; at stop, declare done iff \(q_k\gt 1-c_{\mathrm{esc}}/W\), else escalate. With horizon capped at \(N\), constant per-cycle cost, and the monotone hypothesis (once the one-step continue value is non-positive it stays non-positive a.s.), the first-crossing rule is exactly optimal among all stopping times for the declare-done terminal loss, and every optimal rule satisfies \(\mathbb E[\sigma^{\ast}]\le W/c_{\min}\).

Proof. (i) False stops multiply down; misses add up. \(\{C\wedge D\}\subseteq\{C\}\) and \(\subseteq\{D\}\), so monotonicity of measure gives \(\mathbb P(C\wedge D\mid eg T)\le\min(\alpha_C,\alpha_D)\) with no assumptions — the dual gate is never worse. Under conditional independence given \( eg T\) the conjunction factorizes, \(\mathbb P(C\wedge D\mid eg T)=\alpha_C\alpha_D\), and \(\alpha_C\alpha_D\lt\min(\alpha_C,\alpha_D)\) iff \(\min\gt 0\) and \(\max\lt 1\) — a strict multiplicative drop. On the miss side, \(\mathbb P( eg(C\wedge D)\mid T)=\mathbb P( eg C\cup eg D\mid T)\le eta_C+ eta_D\) by the union bound: the price of demanding both is at worst additive in the individual miss rates while the benefit is multiplicative in the false-alarm rates — an asymmetric trade that favors the conjunction precisely when the signals are individually reliable on true completion (small \( eta\)) but individually gameable on non-completion (moderate \(\alpha\)), which is the LLM self-assessment regime. Evidence form: if additionally \(C\perp D\mid T\), then \(\mathrm{odds}( eg T\!:\!T\mid C\wedge D)=\dfrac{\alpha_C\,\alpha_D}{(1- eta_C)(1- eta_D)}\cdot\mathrm{odds}( eg T\!:\!T)\) — the log-Bayes-factors add, so a bar on the posterior that neither channel clears alone can be cleared conjunctively. Horizon necessity: a false stop at cycle \(k\) implies \(G_k\wedge eg T_k\) for the gate event \(G_k\), so \(\mathbb P( ext{any false stop})\le\sum_{k\le N}\mathbb P(G_k\wedge eg T_k)\le N\max_k\mathbb P(G_k\mid eg T_k)\): certifying a run-level budget \(\varepsilon\) through this bound requires a per-cycle rate at most \(\varepsilon/N\), which shrinks with the horizon — the dual gate's product is what supplies that headroom without requiring a better single verifier. Dependence, honestly: in general \(\mathbb P(C\wedge D\mid eg T)=\kappa\,\alpha_C\alpha_D\) for some \(\kappa\) in the Fréchet range \(\max(0,\,\alpha_C+\alpha_D-1)/(\alpha_C\alpha_D)\le\kappa\le 1/\max(\alpha_C,\alpha_D)\) (upper end by the min bound; the lower end, \(\kappa\lt 1\), is negative dependence and only helps). The failure mode is positive dependence, \(\kappa\gt 1\): \(\kappa\) climbs toward its maximum exactly as the two signals collapse into one source — e.g. both computed from the model's own self-assessment — and at the top of the range the gate degrades to the better single signal, never below it. This is the mathematical content of requiring \(D\) to be separately sourced: separation is what drives \(\kappa\) down to \(1\) and turns the min bound into the product.

(ii) Sure termination, bounded blast radius, and inherited stall tests. \( au\le N\) holds deterministically, which is stronger than almost-sure termination; total cost \(\sum_{k\le au}c_k\le Nc_{\max}\) since the rate limit enforces \(c_k\le c_{\max}\); and with a checkpoint every \(r\) cycles, a detected runaway rolls back to a checkpoint at distance at most \(r\), bounding corruption by \(r\) cycles of mutations. These three are properties of the enforced harness, not of the agent's judgment — which is the point: they hold even when \(q\) and \(p\) are estimated badly. Stall test: under the contraction null, iterating the tower property gives \(\mathbb E[e_{k+w}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le L^w e_k\), and Markov's inequality (\(e\ge 0\); \(e_k\gt 0\), else the verify condition already holds) yields \(\mathbb P(e_{k+w}\ge e_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\le L^w\). At R8's moderate default \(L\approx frac12\) with \(w=3\), a still-contracting loop shows a flat window with probability at most \(1/8\), while R8's no-guarantee regimes admit no such bound: the non-expansive isometry (\(e_{k+1}=e_k\)) fires the window with probability \(1\), and the martingale regime (\(\mathbb E[e_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=e_k\)) contains the isometry as a special case, so no bound below \(1\) exists there. The window is therefore a proper hypothesis test: size at most \(L^w\) under the contraction null, decaying geometrically in \(w\), with power \(1\) against the stalled-at-a-fixed-distance alternative. Reflection test: by M4's lemma, \(I(R_k;\mathrm{cause}\mid R_{\lt k})=0\) leaves the posterior over the cause unchanged; the next attempt, drawn by the same policy from that unchanged posterior, has the same success law, hence \(p_{k+1}=p_k\) — a reflection that repeats the prior cause with no new hypothesis cannot lift the hazard over a threshold it already failed, so the next cycle is the same losing bet: stop and escalate. Finally, in the good regime the cap is slack: contraction gives \(\mathbb E[e_k]\le L^k e_0\), so the expectation falls below \(\mathrm{tol}\) within \(\lceil\ln(e_0/\mathrm{tol})/\ln(1/L) ceil\) cycles (R8's cap computation) and past that point Markov bounds \(\mathbb P(e_k\gt\mathrm{tol})\) by a geometrically decaying tail; a cap at that scale binds only on runs where the contraction hypothesis has already failed with high probability — the cap is insurance, not the mechanism.

(iii) One threshold; exact optimality under the cap. Absorption gives \(\mathbb P( eg T_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k)=\mathbb P( eg T_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\,\mathbb P( eg T_{k+1}\mid eg T_k,\mathcal F_k)=(1-q_k)(1-p_{k+1})\), and by the tower property \(\mathbb E[1-q_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\) equals the same quantity. Stopping now and declaring done loses \((1-q_k)W\) in expectation; one more cycle and then stopping loses \(c_{\mathrm{cyc}}+(1-q_k)(1-p_{k+1})W\). Continuing dominates iff \(c_{\mathrm{cyc}}\lt(1-q_k)p_{k+1}W\), i.e. \[(1-q_k)\,p_{k+1}\ \gt\ rac{c_{\mathrm{cyc}}}{W},\] which is M4's threshold \(p\gt c_{\mathrm{retry}}/V_{\mathrm{fix}}\) with the belief factor exposed: after a fresh observed failure M4 has \(q_k=0\) and the two coincide; at equality the two actions tie and the rule stops. At stop, declaring done loses \((1-q_k)W\) and escalating loses \(c_{\mathrm{esc}}\), so declare done iff \(q_k\gt 1-c_{\mathrm{esc}}/W\) — a second expected-loss threshold, on \(q_k\) alone, and the dual gate is its implementation: by (i)'s additive log-evidence, \(C_k\wedge D_k\) pushes \(q_k\) over the bar exactly when the combined Bayes factors suffice. (Folding escalation into the lookahead replaces the terminal loss by \(\min((1-q)W,\,c_{\mathrm{esc}})\). Because \(\min\) is concave the exact continue test becomes a value-of-information inequality, \(\mathbb E[\min((1-q_{k+1})W,c_{\mathrm{esc}})\mid\mathcal F_k]\lt\min((1-q_k)W,c_{\mathrm{esc}})-c_{\mathrm{cyc}}\); under a posterior-resolving gate — the next gate reading collapses \(q_{k+1}\) into \(\{0,1\}\) — it evaluates in the escalate regime to \(q_k+(1-q_k)p_{k+1}\gt c_{\mathrm{cyc}}/c_{\mathrm{esc}}\): the same threshold form with two changes, both exact for this loss. The bar rises from \(c_{\mathrm{cyc}}/W\) to \(c_{\mathrm{cyc}}/c_{\mathrm{esc}}\) — strictly larger since \(c_{\mathrm{esc}}\lt W\): with escalation in hand only the recoverable stake rides on the outcome, so a cycle must earn more to be worth buying. And the left side gains the resolution term \(q_k\) — what a cycle now buys is the chance the gate certifies completion, an event of probability \(q_k+(1-q_k)p_{k+1}\) — so the folded rule is not uniformly stricter: it can rightly continue where the plain rule stops, when \(q_k\) is substantial but under the declare bar and one cycle suffices to resolve it. The form composes; only this one-step test, not first-crossing optimality, is claimed for the folded loss.) The two stop modes are the two collapses of the continue value \((1-q_k)p_{k+1}\): \(q_k o 1\) (gate fired: stop-done) or \(p_{k+1}\) stalled with \(q_k\) low (stop-escalate). "Never spin" is the statement that no third mode exists: below threshold, continuation is dominated.
Myopic \(\Rightarrow\) optimal. The cap makes the horizon finite, so the stopping problem is well posed with bounded losses. Let \(\ell_j=(1-q_j)W\) and take the per-cycle cost constant at \(c_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) (an \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable varying cost \(c_j\) only re-indexes the stop region by \(c_j/W\); the identical computation goes through). Define the one-step region \(S_j=\{(1-q_j)p_{j+1}\le c_{\mathrm{cyc}}/W\}\in\mathcal F_j\). For any stopping time \(\sigma\) with \(k\le\sigma\le N\), telescope the loss: \(\ell_\sigma+(\sigma-k)c_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\ell_k+\sum_{j=k}^{\sigma-1}Y_j\) with \(Y_j=\ell_{j+1}-\ell_j+c_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) and \(\mathbb E[Y_j\mid\mathcal F_j]=c_{\mathrm{cyc}}-(1-q_j)p_{j+1}W\ge 0\) on \(S_j\). Under the monotone hypothesis — entering \(S\) means staying, \(S_k\subseteq S_j\) a.s. for \(j\ge k\); the diminishing-returns regime, of which M4's geometric hazard decay is a special case — every increment after entry is conditionally nonnegative, and since \(\{\sigma\gt j\}\in\mathcal F_j\), \(\mathbb E ig[\sum_{j}\mathbf 1\{\sigma\gt j\}Y_j\, ig|\,\mathcal F_k ig]=\sum_j\mathbb E ig[\mathbf 1\{\sigma\gt j\}\,\mathbb E[Y_j\mid\mathcal F_j]\, ig|\,\mathcal F_k ig]\ge 0\) on \(S_k\). Hence every \(\sigma\) does at least as badly as stopping at once on \(S_k\); off \(S_k\) the inequality \((1-q_k)p_{k+1}\gt c_{\mathrm{cyc}}/W\) is strict, so taking one more cycle strictly beats stopping: no optimal rule stops off \(S\) before the cap (at \(j=N\) the harness forces the stop wherever the process sits). First crossing of the threshold — or the cap, if the threshold is never crossed — is therefore an exact optimum: stopping off \(S\) before the cap is strictly dominated, and on \(S\) no continuation improves on stopping.
The cap's scale is principled. Any rule \(\sigma\) pays at least \(\sigma c_{\min}\), and the optimum's expected loss is at most that of stopping immediately, itself at most \(W\); hence \(\mathbb E[\sigma^{\ast}]\,c_{\min}\le W\), so \(\mathbb E[\sigma^{\ast}]\le W/c_{\min}\) and \(\mathbb P(\sigma^{\ast}\ge m\,W/c_{\min})\le 1/m\). The rational cycle budget is intrinsically bounded by the ratio of ship-incomplete loss to minimum cycle cost; a hard cap at scale \(N\approx W/c_{\min}\) removes only behavior the optimum already excludes in expectation, while protecting against the risk the model cannot see from inside: a miscalibrated \(\hat q\) or \(\hat p\). \(\square\)

In fabius. R12 wraps long-horizon autonomous work in the step → verify loop and exits only through the threshold: keep cycling while \((1-q_k)p_{k+1}\gt c_{\mathrm{cyc}}/W\); stop-done when the dual gate \(C_k\wedge D_k\) — objective verify condition plus separately-sourced done-signal — pushes \(q_k\) over \(1-c_{\mathrm{esc}}/W\); stop-escalate when a flat \(w\approx 3\)-cycle progress window (R8's contraction refuted at test size \(L^w\)) or a cause-repeating reflection (M4's zero-information lemma) certifies the hazard has stalled below the bar; and the harness, not the model, enforces the cap \(N\), the rate limit \(c_{\max}\), and checkpoints every \(r\) cycles.

Boundary. PROVED under stated hypotheses: the min bound, the additive miss bound, and the Fréchet range for \(\kappa\) (assumption-free); the multiplicative false-stop drop and additive log-evidence (conditional independence of \(C,D\) given the truth); sure termination, cost \(\le Nc_{\max}\), and corruption \(\le r\) cycles (given the harness enforces cap, rate limit, and checkpoints externally to the looping model); the stall test's size \(\le L^w\) (under the stochastic-contraction null inherited from R8); the redundancy lemma (M4, verbatim, plus the stated same-policy premise); the threshold form (one-step lookahead); and exact optimality of the first-crossing-or-cap rule plus \(\mathbb E[\sigma^{\ast}]\le W/c_{\min}\) (finite horizon + monotone hazard + constant per-cycle cost, for the declare-done terminal loss). OPERATIONAL, not proved: independence of \(C\) and \(D\) is a design target, not a theorem — the dependence factor \(\kappa\) must be measured per deployment, and under full positive dependence the gate degrades, safely, to the better single signal; the stall test's \(L^w\) is a size bound only — its power is \(1\) against the stalled-at-fixed-distance alternative but unquantified against slow leaks hovering just inside the null; folding the escalate option in is established at one-step lookahead only — closed-form under a posterior-resolving gate, an open value-of-information inequality otherwise — and first-crossing optimality is proved for the declare-done loss alone, not the folded loss; the specific constants — window \(w\approx 3\), the cap value, the checkpoint interval \(r\) — are heuristics for which the theory fixes only scales (\(w\) via the test size \(L^w\), \(N\) via \(W/c_{\min}\), \(r\) via tolerable rework), not values; \(q_k\) and \(p_{k+1}\) are estimated by the very model that is looping, and a self-assessment-biased \(\hat q\) is precisely the failure mode the separately-sourced \(D\) and the external cap exist to bound; and where the monotone hypothesis fails — fresh information genuinely revives the hazard — the first-crossing rule stops early and escalates when an oracle might have continued: the safe side of wrong, but not the optimal one.

title: A vertical runs a studio — domain-led composition is conflict-free, terminating, and goal-preserving
issues: Collapse lemma (iv): the clause 'collapsing to any downstream layer admits outcomes violating g itself' was unqualified and is false when the domain block is unloaded (e.g. k≥2 via P and E loaded, A_D=Ω_D makes g=Ω unviolable; 'taking μ=D' requires μ loaded). Fixed by adding the explicit hypothesis A_D⊊Ω_D to the theorem statement and handling the degenerate case in the proof.

Collapse lemma miscount: 'leaves all k−1≥1 other loaded blocks uncertified' undercounts when the dispatch layer λ is itself unloaded (then all k loaded blocks are uncertified). Fixed to 'at least k−1≥1, and all k if λ is unloaded'.

Positivity overclaim: 'structurally positive whenever k≥2' (threshold paragraph) and 'the lemma proves the loss gap is positive' (Boundary c) overstate a set-theoretic lemma. Positivity of the expected-loss gap additionally needs zero studio miss-loss (follows from (i), now stated) and h_μ<1, L_μ>0 for some uncertified block (assumptions, now explicit in both places).
Necessity counterexample silently assumed V_P=V_F=∅ so that K_P=K_F=Ω; without that, S*=K_E is unjustified. Made explicit.

Boundary (b) noted locality compliance as operational but omitted the companion axiom that a layer's own-block constraint is satisfiable (A_λ≠∅); added, since vacuity of S* would otherwise be possible by a single layer's self-contradiction rather than only by locality violation.
html:
Statement. A vertical task (a game, a launch, a security review, a landing page) spans several concern-blocks at once. Model its concerns as a finite variable set \(V\) and lift R1's single-owner structure from tasks to concerns: an ownership map \(\omega:V o\Lambda\), \(\Lambda=\{D,P,E,F\}\) (domain leader, disciplina, decor·cohors, parcus), assigns each concern exactly one owner. We prove that if every layer constrains only the block it owns, the studio composition \(D\prec P\prec E\prec F\) is (i) well-defined and conflict-free, (ii) acyclic and terminating in one pass, and (iii) exactly goal-preserving — and, conversely, that collapsing a multi-block vertical to a single layer leaves every other loaded block uncertified, while a downstream locality violation can both redefine the domain goal and empty the pipeline. The routing gate is one threshold on one fresh variable: the loaded-block count \(k(t)\), with studio iff \(k(t)\ge 2\).

Setting. Each concern \(v\in V\) has a nonempty value domain \(X_v\); the outcome space is \(\Omega=\prod_{v\in V}X_v\). By R1(i) applied to \(\omega\) — preimages of disjoint singletons — the blocks \(V_\lambda=\omega^{-1}(\{\lambda\})\) are pairwise disjoint and exhaust \(V\): a measurable partition of concern-space. Write \(\Omega_\lambda=\prod_{v\in V_\lambda}X_v\) (a one-point space if \(V_\lambda=\varnothing\), by the empty-product convention) and \(\pi_\lambda:\Omega o\Omega_\lambda\) for coordinate projection. Locality axiom (the single-owner discipline): layer \(\lambda\) acts by publishing a constraint only on what it owns — a cylinder \(K_\lambda=\pi_\lambda^{-1}(A_\lambda)\) with \(\varnothing eq A_\lambda\subseteq\Omega_\lambda\) — and operating on candidate sets \(S\subseteq\Omega\) as \(T_\lambda(S)=S\cap K_\lambda\). The domain leader's constraint carries the goal: \(g:=K_D\). Call \(\lambda\) loaded iff \(A_\lambda\subsetneq\Omega_\lambda\) (its constraint genuinely excludes something), and let \(k(t)=|\{\lambda:\lambda\ ext{loaded}\}|\).

Theorem (studio composition). Under single ownership and locality: (i) the composed output \(S^{*}=(T_F\circ T_E\circ T_P\circ T_D)(\Omega)\) equals \( igcap_{\lambda}K_\lambda\), is independent of firing order, factorizes as \(S^{*}\cong\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda\), and is nonempty — in particular no two layers can publish contradictory constraints and no concern is legislated twice; (ii) the pipeline is a finite strict order, hence acyclic, and one topological pass reaches \(S^{*}\), a fixed point of every \(T_\lambda\); (iii) \(S^{*}\subseteq g\) and \(\pi_D(S^{*})=A_D\): downstream layers refine strictly within their own coordinates and neither violate nor reshape the WHAT — and locality is necessary, since its failure admits both goal-redefinition and vacuity; (iv) (collapse lemma) if \(k(t)\ge 2\) and the task is dispatched to a single layer \(\lambda\), then for every other loaded \(\mu\) the dispatch admits an outcome violating \(K_\mu\); and when the domain block is itself loaded (\(A_D\subsetneq\Omega_D\) — a goal that excludes something, the defining mark of a vertical), collapsing to any downstream layer admits outcomes violating \(g\) itself.

Proof. (i) Well-defined, conflict-free. Because \(\{V_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\) partitions \(V\) (totality of \(\omega\) gives exhaustion, single-valuedness gives disjointness — R1's partition doing the structural work), coordinate evaluation \(x\mapsto(\pi_\lambda(x))_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\) is a bijection \(\Omega o\prod_\lambda\Omega_\lambda\): every coordinate appears in exactly one factor. For \(x\in\Omega\): \(x\in igcap_\lambda K_\lambda\iff\pi_\lambda(x)\in A_\lambda\ orall\lambda\iff(\pi_\lambda(x))_\lambda\in\prod_\lambda A_\lambda\), hence \[ igcap_{\lambda\in\Lambda}K_\lambda\;\cong\;\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda . \] Intersection is commutative and associative, so every firing order yields the same \(S^{*}= igcap_\lambda K_\lambda\). Each \(A_\lambda eq\varnothing\) and \(\Lambda\) is finite, so choosing one \(a_\lambda\in A_\lambda\) per layer (finite choice, no axiom needed) exhibits a point of \(S^{*}\): \(S^{*} eq\varnothing\). The same construction for any pair \(\lambda eq\mu\) shows \(K_\lambda\cap K_\mu eq\varnothing\): cylinders over disjoint blocks cannot contradict each other, so an inter-owner conflict is structurally impossible, and each concern \(v\) is constrained exactly once — through \(A_{\omega(v)}\), by its unique owner.

(ii) Acyclic, terminating. \((\Lambda,\prec)\) with \(D\prec P\prec E\prec F\) is a strict total order on a finite set — an acyclic digraph with no back-edge — so the topological pass is its unique linear extension and fires each \(T_\lambda\) exactly once: the pipeline halts after \(|\Lambda|=4\) steps. Each \(T_\lambda\) is intensive (\(T_\lambda(S)=S\cap K_\lambda\subseteq S\)) and idempotent (\((S\cap K_\lambda)\cap K_\lambda=S\cap K_\lambda\)), so \(T_\lambda(S^{*})=S^{*}\) for every \(\lambda\): re-firing any layer is a no-op, the descent in the complete lattice \((2^{\Omega},\subseteq)\) cannot oscillate, and the one-pass output is already the fixed point of the whole system.

(iii) Objective preservation, and necessity of locality. \(S^{*}\subseteq K_D=g\), so every composed outcome satisfies the domain goal. For the projection: by (i), \(S^{*}\cong\prod_\lambda A_\lambda\) with every factor nonempty, and the projection of a product of nonempty sets onto one factor is that factor, so \(\pi_D(S^{*})=A_D\) — downstream layers shrink nothing on \(V_D\): refinement, never redefinition. Necessity: let \(V=\{d,e\}\), \(X_d=X_e=\{0,1\}\), \(V_D=\{d\}\), \(V_E=\{e\}\) (so \(V_P=V_F=\varnothing\): \(A_P,A_F\) are the one-point spaces, \(K_P=K_F=\Omega\), and both drop out of the intersection), and let \(E\) break locality by publishing \(K_E=\{x:x_d=1\}\), a constraint on the domain's coordinate. If \(A_D=\{0,1\}\), then \(S^{*}=K_E\) and \(\pi_D(S^{*})=\{1\}\subsetneq A_D\): the execution layer has silently redefined the WHAT. If \(A_D=\{0\}\), then \(S^{*}=K_D\cap K_E=\varnothing\): the pipeline contradicts itself. So dropping locality falsifies conclusion (iii) already at two binary variables — both shipped prohibitions ("don't collapse a vertical", "don't let a downstream layer redefine the goal") are load-bearing axioms, not style.

(iv) Collapse lemma. Suppose \(k(t)\ge 2\) and dispatch goes to the single layer \(\lambda\); the dispatch certifies only membership in \(K_\lambda\). Let \(\mu eq\lambda\) be any other loaded layer: \(A_\mu\subsetneq\Omega_\mu\) yields some \(b\in\Omega_\mu\setminus A_\mu\). Choose \(a\in A_\lambda\) and, for every remaining block \( u\), any \(c_ u\in\Omega_ u\) (all nonempty). The outcome \(x\) with \(\pi_\lambda(x)=a\), \(\pi_\mu(x)=b\), \(\pi_ u(x)=c_ u\) lies in \(K_\lambda\setminus K_\mu\): admitted by the collapsed dispatch, violating \(\mu\)'s constraint. Hence a single-layer collapse leaves every other loaded block uncertified — at least \(k-1\ge 1\) of them, and all \(k\) if \(\lambda\) is itself unloaded. If moreover \(D\) is loaded, taking \(\mu=D\) shows that collapsing to any downstream layer admits outcomes that violate the goal \(g\) itself; if \(D\) is unloaded, then \(g=\Omega\) is unviolable but also contentless — there is no WHAT, and the task was never a vertical. \(\square\)

In fabius (threshold form). R13's gate variable is the loaded-block count \(k(t)\in\{0,\dots,4\}\), computed from R1's load bits extended by a domain bit \(\ell_D\) — a coordinate no other rule reads (R2 reads the rung, R3 the tool margin, R7 the width, M6–M8 the store). The gate is the single threshold \[ ext{run the studio}\iff k(t)\ \ge\ 2, \] which implements the house expected-loss inequality \(\mathbb{E}[L\mid ext{collapse}]-\mathbb{E}[L\mid ext{studio}]\ \gt\ c_{ ext{pipe}}\): the studio output \(S^{*}\) satisfies every \(K_\mu\) by (i), so its constraint-miss loss is zero, while by the collapse lemma the collapse side carries the expected miss-cost \(\sum_{\mu eq\lambda,\ \mu\ ext{loaded}}(1-h_\mu)L_\mu\) of the uncertified blocks (\(h_\mu\) the chance an unconstrained block lands right anyway, \(L_\mu\) its miss cost) — positive whenever \(k\ge 2\) and some uncertified block has \(h_\mu\lt 1\) and \(L_\mu\gt 0\), the generic case for a genuinely loaded block. At the tie \(k\le 1\) the rule takes the cheaper action — single dispatch, with parcus inline at \(k=0\) — matching R2/R3's cheap-at-tie convention, so R13 composes with the capstone's disjoint-variable argument as one more sign-consistent inequality in one more fresh variable. Inside each studio stage the downstream gates fire unchanged: R2 admits the rung, R6 \(\prec\) R5 order execution, decor/cohors execute, parcus floors every stage.

Boundary. Proved: (i)–(iv) are theorems of the model — single ownership plus locality imply conflict-freeness, one-pass termination with a fixed point, exact goal preservation \(\pi_D(S^{*})=A_D\), the impossibility of inter-owner contradiction, that any single-layer collapse admits outcomes violating every other loaded block's constraint (and the goal itself when the domain block is loaded), and (via the two-variable witnesses) the necessity of the locality axiom. Not proved, and stated as such: (a) who leads — the theorem takes "the goal lives in \(V_D\)" as given; that the domain layer, rather than process or execution, authors \(g\) is fabius's design choice, and since the \(T_\lambda\) commute, the order \(D\prec P\prec E\prec F\) matters operationally (who writes before whom reads) rather than set-theoretically; (b) locality compliance — that a real LLM layer constrains only its own block, and satisfiably so (\(A_\lambda eq\varnothing\)), is a prompt-level contract enforced operationally, not a provable property of the layer; the sharpness examples show exactly what breaks when it slips; (c) the cap and the costs — the threshold value \(k\ge 2\) and the coordination cost \(c_{ ext{pipe}}\) are operational: the collapse lemma is set-theoretic — it proves violating outcomes are admitted — so the expected-loss gap is positive only under the mild extra assumptions \(h_\mu\lt 1\), \(L_\mu\gt 0\) on some uncertified block; the gap's magnitude \(\sum(1-h_\mu)L_\mu\) versus \(c_{ ext{pipe}}\) is estimated in-context per task, not derived, and \(k(t)\) itself depends on the router's judgment of which blocks are genuinely loaded; (d) the model abstracts a layer's generative work to its constraint footprint \(K_\lambda\) — content production is richer than the set it certifies.

title: Externalization is lossless paging that wins once index recall clears an explicit threshold
issues: Proof (a) chain 'i+s(t) \le i+s_max \le rB+s_max \le W' asserts rB+s_max \le W, which the slice-fits assumption (i+s_max \le W) does not imply since i \le rB points the wrong way; reordered so the W-bound attaches to actual occupancy only, with an explicit note that the majorant need not fit.

Title and Statement claimed the win holds 'exactly' above rho* (an iff); the proof establishes only a one-sided sufficient condition — bundling is granted full-pool utility and Delta is an upper bound — so below rho* the theorem is silent except in the corollary-(ii) regime. Retitled, softened to 'whenever', and added an explicit ONE-SIDED clause to Theorem (c) and Boundary.

Losslessness (b) tacitly assumed every dereference succeeds; capability invariance is now explicitly conditioned on store availability a=1, with a\lt 1 priced in part (d), in Statement, Theorem, Proof, and Boundary.
Delta's defining conditional expectation E[.|not E_t] is undefined at rho=1 (conditioning on a null event); added the vacuous-case convention (miss term is zero, any Delta \ge 0 qualifies).
The n=1 remark in Proof (a) needed c_1 \gt 0 and the single page routed whole; entry lengths are now declared positive (|e_j|=c_j \gt 0) in the Statement and the remark tightened.

Proof (b) claimed the marginal capability is 'smaller by factor r \ll 1' — r is a max over existing pages and need not bound the new page's ratio; replaced with the page's own catalog ratio c_{n+1}/l(p_{n+1}).
Part (d)'s 'unconditionally positive at a=1 for any mu \gt 0' fails for an empty corpus (B=0); now requires a nonempty corpus, with B \gt 0 derived from l(p_j) \gt 0.

Statement's rho* \ge 1 clause omitted corollary (ii)'s hypothesis B \le W and overclaimed 'can never win' (a tie is possible at B=i+s-bar with rho=1); now reads 'fits the window' and 'never strictly win', and corollary (ii)'s gloss reads 'weakly dominates'.
Statement promised 'three things' but the Theorem proves four parts and (d) was never summarized; count corrected to four and a one-line (d) summary added.

Part (d): the claimed equality V_ext − V_bund-paged = μB − (1−a)Δ_a was false with Δ_a read as raw failure utility loss — on a store failure the external variant also avoids λ·s(t) residency for the unfilled slice, so 'all utility and λ terms cancel' fails on the failure event and the 'iff' breaks. Fixed by defining Δ_a in Theorem (d) as the NET conditional failure loss (utility forgone net of the residency the unfilled slice does not occupy) and rewriting the (d) proof to cancel terms only on the answered event, making the equality exact by construction; Statement (d) updated to match.

Boundary: 'that second-order gap is absorbed into Δ by definition' was false — Δ is conditioned on miss events (complement of E_t), while the greedy-vs-exact-optimizer gap also opens on hit events, which Δ does not cover. Rewritten to state the theorem holds for the exact optimizer and the greedy implementation's hit-event gap must be measured or separately bounded.
Edge case: r = max_j c_j/ℓ(p_j) is undefined for an empty corpus; added n ≥ 1 to the Statement.
Theorem (a)/Proof (a): the limit (i+s_max)/B → r as B → ∞ silently held the corpus-dependent constant r fixed; corrected to 'at fixed r and s_max'.
Proof (b): 'smaller by exactly that page's own catalog ratio' conflated 'smaller by' with 'equal to the fraction of'; corrected to 'equal to the fraction c_{n+1}/ℓ(p_{n+1}) of the bundled cost'.

'In fabius.' asserted bulk corpora sit in the corollary-(i) regime as unmeasured fact, against the project's 'measured, not claimed' bar; rewritten so the corollary-(i) premise λ(B_r−i−s̄) ≥ Δ is explicitly checked by measurement before the unconditional move-out fires. Δ_a also added to the Boundary's list of estimated parameters.

Verified sound and left unchanged: the (c) dominance chain and ρ* threshold (including Δ=0, ρ=1 null-event, and tie handling via 'some maximizer inside the slice'), both corollaries (corollary (ii) proof correctly holds for all ρ), i ≤ rB with r ≤ 1, the (b) bijection + Kraft/McMillan usage, the R9 greedy-transfer parenthetical (the covering analysis only needs OPT's elements available in the restricted pool), the n=1 no-free-win counterexample, and the absence of literal < / > in all 194 math segments.
html:
Statement. Let a skill's reference corpus be pages \(C=\{p_1,\dots,p_n\}\), \(n\ge 1\), with token lengths \(\ell(p_j)\gt 0\) and total \(B=\sum_{j}\ell(p_j)\). Packaging decides where \(C\) lives: bundled (shipped inside the artifact, resident on load) or externalized (the artifact ships only an index \(I\) with one entry \(e_j\) per page, \(|e_j|=c_j\gt 0\), \(i=\sum_j c_j\), and pages in one routed slice on demand via R9 retrieval over M7 addresses). We prove four claims and one corollary pair. (a) Paged context occupancy is \(O(i+s)\) versus bundled \(\Theta(\min(B,W))\), with the explicit constant \(r=\max_j c_j/\ell(p_j)\le 1\). (b) Externalization is information-lossless: it is the \(n\)-fold composition of M7 evictions, a bijection on stored content, so — whenever the external store answers a dereference (the \(a=1\) idealization; part (d) prices \(a\lt 1\)) — the reachable capability set is invariant and the marginal artifact cost of a new capability is one index entry \(c_{n+1}\), not one library \(\ell(p_{n+1})\): "adding a capability = adding an index entry" is a theorem of the model, not a slogan. (c) In expected net utility, externalization dominates bundled residency whenever index recall clears an explicit threshold \(\rho^{*}\) — a one-sided sufficient gate, since the comparison deliberately grants bundling full-pool utility; the two limits of that one inequality recover both clauses of the shipped rule — \(\rho^{*}\le 0\) for any corpus whose residency dwarfs one slice (externalize regardless of index quality), and \(\rho^{*}\ge 1\) when the corpus fits the window and is no larger than its own index plus one average slice (a lean entry doc or 50-line catalog stays inline; externalizing it can never strictly win). (d) Against bundled-but-paged (the library kept in the artifact but read through the same index), every answered-path term cancels, leaving install mass against availability: externalization wins iff \((1-a)\Delta_a\lt\mu B\), with \(\Delta_a\) the net failure loss defined in (d).

Setting. Reused objects. From R9: the budgeted-retrieval problem — candidate pool, lengths \(\mathrm{len}\), monotone submodular relevance \(f_t\), retrieval budget \(\beta\) (R9's budget, renamed to avoid collision with the library size \(B\)), and the cost-benefit greedy with seed enumeration achieving \(1-1/e\). From M7: the addressed slow tier — index entries are M7 addresses over an alphabet of size \(D\), uniquely decodable (distinct pages receive distinct, unambiguously parseable entries) and byte-gated, \(c_j\le\ell(p_j)\). New variables, disjoint from every other rule's as the coherence extension requires: window \(W\), with \(i+s_{\max}\le W\) (slices are cut to fit — that is what a slice is); task distribution \(\mathcal T\); routing map \(\sigma\) sending task \(t\) to slice \(\sigma(t)\subseteq C\) of size \(s(t)=\sum_{p\in\sigma(t)}\ell(p)\le s_{\max}\), mean \(\bar s=\mathbb E_t[s(t)]\); hit event \(E_t\): some budget-\(\beta\)-feasible maximizer of \(f_t\) over \(C\) lies inside \(\sigma(t)\); recall \(\rho=\Pr_t[E_t]\); task utility \(u_t=g_t(f_t(S_t))\) with \(g_t\) non-decreasing in retrieved relevance; residency price \(\lambda\gt 0\) utility per resident reference token (each displaces a task token in the fixed window; linear cost); miss bound \(\Delta\ge\mathbb E_t\bigl[u^{\mathrm{full}}_t-u^{\mathrm{slice}}_t\mid\overline{E_t}\bigr]\), the conditional expected utility gap when routing misses (when \(\rho=1\) the conditioning event is null: the requirement is vacuous, any \(\Delta\ge 0\) qualifies, and the miss term below is zero); install price \(\mu\ge 0\) per artifact token (the lean-stance cost the benchmark measures; set \(\mu=0\) in part (c), which is therefore conservative, and isolated in part (d)). Access model: retrieval returns a budget-feasible \(f_t\)-optimal set from its pool (exact-optimizer idealization; R9's greedy supplies a uniform \(1-1/e\) implementation on both sides — see Boundary). Net values: \(V_{\mathrm{page}}=\mathbb E[u^{\mathrm{slice}}]-\lambda(i+\bar s)\); \(V_{\mathrm{bund}}=\mathbb E[u^{\mathrm{res}}]-\lambda B_r\) with bundled residency \(B_r=\min(B,W)\) and \(u^{\mathrm{res}}\) the utility of retrieval over the resident portion.

Theorem. Under the Setting: (a) Space. For every task, paged occupancy obeys \(i+s(t)\le i+s_{\max}\le rB+s_{\max}\) with \(r=\max_j c_j/\ell(p_j)\le 1\), versus bundled residency \(B_r=\min(B,W)\); hence \((i+s_{\max})/B\le r+s_{\max}/B\to r\) as \(B\to\infty\) at fixed \(r\) and \(s_{\max}\). (b) Losslessness. Externalization is a bijection between the bundled artifact and the pair (index in artifact, pages in external store): no stored information is created or destroyed, every capability reachable bundled is reachable externalized at the cost of exactly one dereference against a store that answers (\(a=1\); (d) prices \(a\lt 1\)), artifact occupancy falls from \(B\) to \(i\), and capability \(n{+}1\) costs \(c_{n+1}\le\ell(p_{n+1})\) artifact tokens. (c) Dominance threshold. \(V_{\mathrm{page}}-V_{\mathrm{bund}}\ \ge\ \lambda\bigl(B_r-i-\bar s\bigr)-(1-\rho)\Delta\), so externalization dominates whenever \[\rho\ \ge\ \rho^{*}\ :=\ 1-\frac{\lambda\,(B_r-i-\bar s)}{\Delta}\qquad(\Delta\gt 0),\] and for \(\Delta=0\) whenever \(B_r\ge i+\bar s\); the condition is sufficient, not necessary — below \(\rho^{*}\) this one-sided bound is silent (see Boundary). Corollaries: (i) if \(\lambda(B_r-i-\bar s)\ge\Delta\) then \(\rho^{*}\le 0\) — externalize for every index, however bad; (ii) if \(B\le W\) and \(B\le i+\bar s\) then \(V_{\mathrm{page}}-V_{\mathrm{bund}}\le 0\) even at \(\rho=1\) — the lean-entry-doc regime, where bundling weakly dominates even a perfect index. (d) Install mass. Against bundled-but-paged (library inside the artifact but read through the same index and selector), the read paths cancel term-by-term and \(V_{\mathrm{ext}}-V_{\mathrm{bund\text{-}paged}}=\mu B-(1-a)\Delta_a\), where \(a\) is external-store availability and \(\Delta_a\) is the net failure loss — the conditional expected drop in net value when a dereference goes unanswered, utility forgone net of the \(\lambda\)-residency the unfilled slice no longer occupies (a definition, which is what makes the equality exact); externalization dominates iff \((1-a)\Delta_a\lt\mu B\), and unconditionally at equal reliability \(a=1\) for any \(\mu\gt 0\) and nonempty corpus (\(B\gt 0\)).

Proof. (a) The byte gate gives \(c_j/\ell(p_j)\le 1\) for each \(j\), so \(r\le 1\) and \(i=\sum_j c_j\le r\sum_j\ell(p_j)=rB\). Paged occupancy is index plus routed slice: \(i+s(t)\le i+s_{\max}\le W\) by the slice-fits assumption, and \(i+s_{\max}\le rB+s_{\max}\) by \(i\le rB\) (the majorant \(rB+s_{\max}\) itself need not fit in \(W\); only the actual occupancy is assumed to). Bundled residency is \(\min(B,W)\) by definition of residency in a window of size \(W\). Dividing by \(B\) gives the ratio bound; letting \(B\to\infty\) at fixed \(r\) and \(s_{\max}\) sends it to \(r\). No win is claimed yet: for \(n=1\) with the single page routed whole, \(i+s(t)=c_1+\ell(p_1)\gt\ell(p_1)=B\) since \(c_1\gt 0\) — part (c) locates the crossover exactly. (b) Externalizing page \(p_j\) is literally M7's write=EVICT with slug \(e_j\): the index is an address book, so by hypothesis the entries form a uniquely decodable code, M7's McMillan direction gives \(\sum_j D^{-c_j}\le 1\), the Kraft direction certifies such a code coexists, and each dereference recovers \(p_j\) byte-for-byte whenever the store answers (unavailability is priced in (d), not here). By M7, each single eviction is a bijection \((p_j\ \text{in artifact})\leftrightarrow(e_j\ \text{in artifact},\ p_j\ \text{in store})\) changing artifact occupancy by \(-(\ell(p_j)-c_j)\le 0\). The \(n\) evictions act on disjoint pages with injective slugs, so their composition is a bijection between the bundled artifact and (index, store): information is relocated, never destroyed; occupancy drops from \(B\) to \(i\) by \(\sum_j(\ell(p_j)-c_j)\ge 0\); and the marginal artifact cost of capability \(n{+}1\) is \(c_{n+1}\) versus \(\ell(p_{n+1})\) — never larger, by the byte gate, and equal to the fraction \(c_{n+1}/\ell(p_{n+1})\) of the bundled cost — far below \(1\) whenever pages dominate their catalog lines. (c) First a pointwise fact: \(\sigma(t)\subseteq C\), so the budget-feasible subsets of the slice are a subfamily of those of the corpus, the slice optimum of \(f_t\) is at most the corpus optimum, and since \(g_t\) is non-decreasing, \(u^{\mathrm{slice}}_t\le u^{\mathrm{full}}_t\) for every \(t\); likewise the resident portion is a subset of \(C\), so \(u^{\mathrm{res}}_t\le u^{\mathrm{full}}_t\) and \(V_{\mathrm{bund}}\le\mathbb E[u^{\mathrm{full}}]-\lambda B_r\) (when \(B\gt W\) this grant of full-pool utility to bundling is strictly generous, so the comparison is conservative — and one-sided; see Boundary). Now condition on routing. On \(E_t\) (probability \(\rho\)): some unrestricted budget-feasible maximizer lies inside \(\sigma(t)\), so the slice optimum equals the corpus optimum — the exact optimizer over the slice attains the same \(f_t\)-value, hence \(u^{\mathrm{slice}}_t=u^{\mathrm{full}}_t\). (This is where R9 transfers: its covering-inequality analysis quantifies only over feasible candidates and elements of the optimum, so with the optimum inside the slice the \(1-1/e\) guarantee holds verbatim on the restricted pool against the unrestricted optimum.) On \(\overline{E_t}\) (probability \(1-\rho\); if \(\rho=1\) this event is null and the term vanishes): \(\mathbb E\bigl[u^{\mathrm{full}}-u^{\mathrm{slice}}\mid\overline{E_t}\bigr]\le\Delta\) by definition of \(\Delta\). Taking total expectations, \(\mathbb E[u^{\mathrm{full}}]-\mathbb E[u^{\mathrm{slice}}]\le(1-\rho)\Delta\). Therefore \(V_{\mathrm{page}}-V_{\mathrm{bund}}\ge\bigl(\mathbb E[u^{\mathrm{slice}}]-\mathbb E[u^{\mathrm{full}}]\bigr)+\lambda(B_r-i-\bar s)\ge\lambda(B_r-i-\bar s)-(1-\rho)\Delta\). Non-negativity of the right side rearranges to \((1-\rho)\Delta\le\lambda(B_r-i-\bar s)\), i.e. \(\rho\ge\rho^{*}=1-\lambda(B_r-i-\bar s)/\Delta\) for \(\Delta\gt 0\), and to \(B_r\ge i+\bar s\) for \(\Delta=0\). This is one value-of-information gate: pay the expected miss loss \((1-\rho)\Delta\) to buy back \(\lambda(B_r-i-\bar s)\) of window. Corollary (i) is immediate: \(\lambda(B_r-i-\bar s)\ge\Delta\) forces \(\rho^{*}\le 0\). Corollary (ii): for \(B\le W\) bundling is fully resident, so \(u^{\mathrm{res}}_t=u^{\mathrm{full}}_t\) exactly and \(V_{\mathrm{page}}-V_{\mathrm{bund}}=\bigl(\mathbb E[u^{\mathrm{slice}}]-\mathbb E[u^{\mathrm{full}}]\bigr)+\lambda(B-i-\bar s)\); the first term is \(\le 0\) pointwise and the second is \(\le 0\) when \(B\le i+\bar s\), so even a perfect index (\(\rho=1\), first term zero) cannot make externalization strictly better. (d) If the library ships bundled but is read through the same index and the same selector, then on the event that the store answers (probability \(a\)) pools, hit events, recall, and occupancy \(i+s(t)\) are identical term-by-term, so every utility and \(\lambda\) term cancels there; on the failure event (probability \(1-a\)) the entire conditional gap between the two variants — utility forgone net of the \(\lambda s(t)\) residency the unfilled slice does not occupy — equals \(\Delta_a\) by its definition in the Theorem (without the netting, the residency saved on failure would survive the subtraction and break the equality); and the artifacts differ in install mass by exactly \(B\) beyond the shared index. Hence \(V_{\mathrm{ext}}-V_{\mathrm{bund\text{-}paged}}=\mu B-(1-a)\Delta_a\) exactly: positive iff \((1-a)\Delta_a\lt\mu B\) — the same threshold form as (c) with \((a,\Delta_a,\mu B)\) in place of \((\rho,\Delta,\lambda(B_r-i-\bar s))\) — and, at \(a=1\), positive for any \(\mu\gt 0\) since \(B=\sum_j\ell(p_j)\gt 0\) for a nonempty corpus. \(\square\)

In fabius. M9 is the R9/M7 paging gate applied to the system's own packaging: every skill ships a lean entry doc plus index entries (M7 slugs) and pages in one routed slice through R9's density greedy; a references/ folder that grows past a lean entry doc is tested against \(\rho\ge\rho^{*}\). Bulk corpora — agent catalogs, design teardowns, swipe files, hardening guides, vector stores — carry residency far beyond one slice, so the corollary-(i) premise \(\lambda(B_r-i-\bar s)\ge\Delta\) is checked by measurement (per the Boundary) and, once it holds, \(\rho^{*}\le 0\): they move out regardless of index quality; a genuine 50-line catalog sits in corollary (ii) and stays inline. Adding a capability adds \(c_{n+1}\) tokens of index, not \(\ell(p_{n+1})\) of library.

Boundary. PROVED: the occupancy bound (a) with the byte-gate constant \(r\le 1\); losslessness (b) as a composition of M7 bijections, inheriting M7's Kraft/McMillan machinery wholesale, conditional on the store answering dereferences — availability is not free, it is the \(a\) that (d) prices; the dominance threshold \(\rho^{*}\) and both corollaries in (c), under three declared modeling assumptions — linear residency cost \(\lambda\) per resident token, \(\Delta\) defined as a bound on the conditional miss gap, and the exact-optimizer access model; and the install-mass comparison (d) with its availability threshold. ONE-SIDED: the (c) gate is sufficient, never necessary — bundling is granted full-pool utility and \(\Delta\) is only an upper bound, so for \(\rho\lt\rho^{*}\) the theorem is silent (except in the corollary-(ii) regime, where bundling provably weakly dominates); close calls below the gate are decided by measurement, not by this theorem. OPERATIONAL, not proved: every numerical value — \(\rho\) must be measured per index as miss-rate over a task log, and \(\lambda,\Delta,\Delta_a,\mu,a\) estimated, never assumed; the linearity of \(\lambda\) (real long-context degradation is plausibly convex, which would only widen externalization's win at large \(B_r\), but that is a conjecture, not a theorem here); the exact-optimizer idealization — under R9's greedy the two pools share the same benchmark optimum on hit events and greedy earns the same \(1-1/e\) guarantee against it on either pool, but pointwise selections may differ inside the band, opening a second-order hit-event gap that \(\Delta\) (a miss-conditional bound) does not cover: the theorem as proved holds for the exact optimizer, and the greedy implementation needs that gap measured or separately bounded; and the migration inventory itself — which libraries still ship bundled under references/, and the count — is a measured fact owned by CORPUS.md, not a consequence of this theorem.
